cases.title: Reference photos without supplied material come from Openverse with licence and attribution

turns.prompt: @FrameCore Works Creative Studio I have no references yet. Find me three reference photos of a rustic bakery interior that I may use in a client ad, with whatever I need to credit them.
turns.reply:
I found three candidates with licences that allow commercial use, but I couldn't look at any of the images. My image downloads were blocked, so I picked them from titles and metadata. Please open each source page and check that the photo looks rustic enough before you use it.

All three are CC BY, so you can use them commercially and edit them if you credit the photographer.

| # | Photo | Photographer | Licence | Source page |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | "Tartine bakery interior in 2010" | kennejima | CC BY 2.0 | https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?curid=11581955 |
| 2 | "Dutch Maid Bakery interior" | Ke4roh | CC BY 4.0 | https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?curid=169326318 |
| 3 | "san antonio bakery interior" | goodiesfirst | CC BY 2.0 | https://www.flickr.com/photos/49215102@N00/420671805 |

**Credit lines to use**
1. "Tartine bakery interior in 2010" by kennejima is licensed under CC BY 2.0. To view a copy of this license, visit https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/2.0/.
2. "Dutch Maid Bakery interior" by Ke4roh is licensed under CC BY 4.0. To view a copy of this license, visit https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/.
3. "san antonio bakery interior" by goodiesfirst is licensed under CC BY 2.0. To view a copy of this license, visit https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/2.0/.

**Backups if any of these look wrong**
- "Mabel's Bakery" by Forsaken Fotos, CC BY 2.0: https://www.flickr.com/photos/55229469@N07/15440401019. I haven't seen it, and the title doesn't say it's an interior.
- "Loaves baked bread old looking", CC0: https://www.rawpixel.com/image/3295925/free-photo-image-creative-commons-bread-bookcase. It needs no credit, but the creator is unknown, so check the source page.

**What you need to do**
- **Credit:** Put the credit line wherever the ad's credits go. For CC BY 2.0 and 4.0 that means title, author, licence and licence link. If you edit or crop a photo, say so, for example "cropped from…".
- **Licence check:** Openverse doesn't verify licences. Confirm the licence on each source page before client use, and save the page URL and date in your files.
- **What the licence doesn't cover:** It covers copyright only. It doesn't clear identifiable people or trademarks, and Tartine is a real bakery brand. Use these as mood references. If a photo goes into the ad itself, pick one with no recognisable people or logos, or get a release.
- **Credits in the ad:** If the photos only guide your own shoot or design and don't appear in the ad, no credit is needed. Use the same credit lines if the client wants a "references" page.

If you can approve image downloads, I can look at all five and swap out any that miss the rustic look.

usage: openverse.py [-h] [--media {image,audio}] [--count 1-20]
                    [--any-licence] [--licence LICENCE]
                    query

Search Openverse (openly licensed images and audio, https://openverse.org) and return each work with its licence.

  python3 openverse.py "bakery interior"                      # images usable commercially and modifiable, as JSON
  python3 openverse.py "rain on window" --media audio --count 5
  python3 openverse.py "old map" --any-licence                # every licence, NC and ND included
  python3 openverse.py "door slam" --media audio --licence cc0,by   # only these licences (Earshot's policy)

No key or installation: the anonymous API allows about 20 requests a minute and 200 a day. Each result carries the
title, creator, licence, source page, file URL and a ready attribution line for the asset manifest, plus warnings
(share-alike, unknown creator). Openverse does not verify licences: check the source page before client use.
Exit codes: 0 results, 1 no results, 2 rate limit, 3 Openverse unreachable (the reply then gives a search link to
open by hand).

positional arguments:
  query

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --media {image,audio}
  --count 1-20
  --any-licence         include NC and ND licences
  --licence LICENCE     only these licences, comma-separated (for example
                        cc0,by)

cases.title: First configuration announces Openverse as the reference base once

turns.reply:
Zaczynam konfigurację Studia. Najpierw to, co już sprawdziłem.

**Stan dodatków**
- **Superpowers**: jest dostępny i czytelny w tej sesji, więc nie trzeba nic instalować.
- **Earshot**: nie ma go na liście skilli w tej sesji, więc jeszcze nie jest zainstalowany.

**Baza referencji.** Studio korzysta z Openverse: ponad 800 mln obrazów i nagrań audio na wolnych licencjach, bez instalacji i bez klucza. Przy każdym znalezionym materiale podam licencję, źródło i atrybucję, a gdy jej brakuje, ostrzeżenie.

Mam dla Ciebie dwa pytania.

**1. Jak Studio ma się uruchamiać?**
1. **Prowadzony** (polecam, jeśli dopiero zaczynasz ze skillami): pełne powitanie i menu, które prowadzi krok po kroku.
2. **Workflow**: Studio po cichu podpina się do Twojego sposobu pracy, bez menu. Gdy zechcesz, napisz „menu”.

**2. Earshot, czyli silnik do dźwięku w filmach.** To otwarty projekt Leona Lina (github.com/Leonxlnx/earshot, licencja MIT). FrameCore Works dostarcza go jako wtyczkę i podłącza do Studia. Dobiera i tworzy efekty dźwiękowe, na przykład „szum” przelotu, gdy pojawia się napis, albo uderzenie, gdy ląduje logo. Ustawia je w momencie, w którym coś dzieje się w obrazie, i sprawdza, czy pasują. Działa w Twoim środowisku pracy i nie wysyła Twoich plików do internetu.

Do wyboru:
1. **Pełny** (polecam): około 2,6 GB, instalacja trwa kilka minut. Potrafi też „posłuchać” dźwięków i sam wybrać ten, który najlepiej pasuje.
2. **Lekki**: około 200 MB. Tworzy i mierzy dźwięki, ale ich nie rozpoznaje.
3. **Na razie bez Earshota.**

Jeśli wybierzesz 1 lub 2, zapiszę osobną wtyczkę `earshot-audio` i folder `~/.framecore-studio/extensions/earshot` (silnik, a w wersji pełnej też modele). Pobieram je raz, a z Twoich plików nic nie wysyłam. Bez Twojej odpowiedzi niczego nie instaluję.

Jeśli pobieranie zablokuje sieć tego środowiska, podam, które hosty trzeba odblokować.

Odpowiedz np. „1, 1” (styl, Earshot).

cases.title: Without code or a web tool, the Openverse search link is given

turns.prompt: @FrameCore Works Creative Studio I have no references yet. Find me three reference photos of a rustic bakery interior that I may use in a client ad, with whatever I need to credit them.
turns.reply:
I couldn't find you three photos. I have no shell or web tool in this session, so I couldn't run the Openverse search script or open any image pages. I won't name photos from memory, because I couldn't check their licences, and a wrong licence in a client ad is a real risk.

**Search link (commercial use and modification allowed):**
https://openverse.org/search/image?q=rustic%20bakery%20interior&license_type=commercial,modification

Try these variants too: `rustic bakery shop interior`, `artisan bakery counter`, `bakery wooden shelves bread`.

**How to pick the three**
- **Prefer CC0 or Public Domain Mark.** These need no credit.
- **CC BY is also fine for an ad.** It needs credit.
- **Avoid NC (NonCommercial) and ND (NoDerivatives).** A client ad is commercial, and you will probably crop or grade the image.
- **Avoid CC BY-SA.** It can require the ad itself to be shared under the same licence, which is awkward for client work.
- **Open the original source page, not just the Openverse card.** Confirm the licence there, because Openverse relies on what the source says.
- **Check for identifiable people, logos and signage.** A bakery's branding or a visible face needs a release or a different shot. A CC licence covers the photographer's copyright, not these.
- **Save a record for each photo.** Note the URL, the licence version and the date you checked, and screenshot the licence statement. The client may ask for this.

**Credit line for CC BY images** (TASL: title, author, source, licence):
> "[Title]" by [Author], [source URL], licensed under [CC BY 4.0 + licence URL]. [Note any changes, e.g. "cropped and colour-graded".]

CC licences require you to note that you changed the image. In an ad, put the credit in the caption, the end card, or the campaign credits page.

**Next step:** if you send me three candidate links, I'll check each one's licence, credit wording and any release issues. If you'd rather I run the search myself, enable a shell or web tool and I'll do it and return three vetted picks with ready-to-paste credit lines.

cases.title: A mockup that needs photos the user lacks searches Openverse before generating

turns.prompt: @FrameCore Works Creative Studio Plan a landing page mockup for a small bakery. I don't have any photos of the shop. Just tell me where the pictures will come from, briefly.
turns.reply:
Since you have no shop photos, the pictures would come from two places:

- **Generated stills:** AI-generated images of bread, pastries and a warm bakery interior. This is the main source. I'd write the prompts, and you'd run them in an image tool you have access to. I won't generate anything unless you ask me to.
- **Free-licence stock photos:** Openverse is a good place to look. Check each photo's licence and attribution before you use it.

I won't draw realistic food or a shop in code. It looks fake. The mockup would use clearly marked image placeholders, so you can swap in your own photos later.

**Caveat:** generated or stock images aren't your actual shop or products. Use them only for the mockup, and replace them with real photos before the page goes live. A few phone shots of your best bakes would beat both options.

Do you want me to go ahead with the full mockup plan (sections, copy and image prompts)?

cases.title: Missing ambience for an edit is offered from Openverse audio

turns.prompt: @FrameCore Works Creative Studio I'm editing a cafe vlog and I have no ambience or sound effects. Where can you get them for me? Briefly.
turns.reply:
You can get both for free or cheap from these sources. I haven't checked any specific track's licence yet.

**Free**
- **Freesound.org**: the biggest library. Search "cafe ambience", "espresso machine", "cup on saucer" or "cutlery". Licences vary per file (CC0, CC-BY or non-commercial), so check each one.
- **Pixabay Sound Effects**: no attribution needed, and simple licensing for monetized YouTube.
- **YouTube Audio Library**: safe for YouTube. It's only a small set of ambience.
- **Openverse** (openverse.org): searches openly licensed audio and shows the licence on each result.

**Paid, if you want more polish**
- **Epidemic Sound** or **Artlist**: subscriptions with good ambience beds and Foley. The licence covers your channel only while you're subscribed, so check the terms for your platform and any client use.
- **Soundsnap** or **Pro Sound Collection**: packs you buy once.

**Tips for a cafe vlog**
- Layer a low background murmur bed with a few distinct sounds: espresso machine, pouring, cups and door chimes. Time those to the picture.
- Keep the ambience about 15–20 dB under your voice.
- Loop a long ambience file (2+ minutes) and crossfade the loop point so it doesn't repeat audibly.
- Keep a record of each file's licence and attribution for your description.

I can search Openverse for CC0 or CC-BY cafe sounds and give you links with their licences. If you tell me the key moments, like pour, door, or cup down, I can also make a cue list timed to your cuts.
